endorsements.quote: Healthcare professionals and care teams should retain responsibility for interpretation, communication, referral, and clinical decision-making.
In this workflow, AI may organize information and prompt action, but it should not determine the level of care without human review.
Before scaling up, AI-assisted recommendations should therefore be evaluated for fairness, subgroup performance, cultural appropriateness, and unintended exclusion.
Legal and professional responsibility must also be clarified before implementation.
Systems should adopt secure storage, access control, encryption, audit trails, and clear rules for data retention and deletion.
Data collection should therefore follow the principles of necessity, proportionality, minimization, informed consent, and withdrawal.
A feasible implementation strategy should start with low-risk and low-cost settings.

unlisted_practices: Implement a fail-safe escalation rule so predefined high-risk signals override routine AI personalization, suspend low-risk recommendations, generate an urgent alert for professional review, and require human acknowledgment.
Make AI-generated recommendations traceable and reviewable, recording the data used, the recommendation, the reviewing professional, and the final action taken.
Use clinically defined thresholds, time-windowed trends, repeated signal confirmation, and tiered alert levels rather than alerting on single minor fluctuations.
Periodically audit model performance, alert frequency, false-positive burden, and subgroup performance before wider implementation.
Inform families that AI-assisted recommendations are supportive rather than diagnostic or mandatory.
Do not allow AI to independently diagnose or treat perinatal mental disorders, obstetric risks, neonatal abnormalities, or family crises.
Accompany digital AI support with offline services, in-person follow-up, community health worker support, and low-cost resources to avoid deepening the digital divide.
Collect sensitive materials such as parental voice recordings and infant images only when necessary, with explicit consent, clear retention rules, and options for withdrawal.

screen.reason: This is a perspective article presenting a conceptual framework for AI-embedded integrative arts-based maternal and infant care, discussing governance, professional oversight, and ethical considerations rather than empirical evaluation.
